Imaging Studies:    CT scan of temporal bones:    Title: Axial Computed Tomographic Scan of Temporal Bone 1 Day After Aural Irrigation    Description: Shows fluid in the left middle ear and mastoid air cells, without evidence of bone erosion. Normal external auditory canal.  
Audiological Tests:    Title: Audiogram and Tympanogram 3 Years After Aural Irrigation    Description: Shows mixed sensorineural and conductive hearing loss in the left ear. Tympanometry in the left ear confirms a high volume owing to tympanic membrane perforation.

bindings.label: Patient developed left facial palsy with lagophthalmos and weak smile (House-Brackman V)
A woman in her 70s presented with impacted cerumen in the right ear, and a practice nurse performed two attempts at bilateral ear irrigation.
Immediately after syringing, the patient reported pain and hearing loss in the left ear, and subsequently developed purulent and blood-stained discharge in that ear.

ENT examination found severe otitis externa with inflammation of the external auditory canal precluding tympanic membrane view; after removal of the wick, a small anteroinferior tympanic membrane perforation was visualized.
Left facial palsy examination showed lagophthalmos, good static tone of the mouth, and weak movement on smiling, graded as House-Brackman V.
CT shows fluid in the left middle ear and mastoid without bone erosion
Audiometry confirms tympanic membrane perforation and mixed hearing loss
Left facial palsy is secondary to otitis externa with middle ear involvement and likely procedural trauma
Microbiological cultures and inflammatory markers remain unavailable despite repeated attempts, so active infection cannot be microbiologically confirmed.
